options.text: Friction between the car and each surface opposes the motion, and it is greater on the rougher doormat.
Friction on the doormat pulls the car forward so it travels farther there than on the tiles.
Friction slows the car on the doormat even if the car's wheels never touch the mat.
Friction opposes motion only on coir mats, never on smooth tiles.

stem:
Ira pushes the same plastic toy car across a smooth tiled corridor and then across a rough coconut-coir doormat. On the doormat the car travels a shorter distance before it stops.

Which claim is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Friction between contacting surfaces opposes motion and is greater on rougher surfaces, so the car stops sooner on the doormat. It does not pull the car forward, act without contact, or apply only on coir.
